overview: This study note explores the practical application of Romans 12, focusing on the dedication of the believer's life through the mind, will, and body, and how these internal states relate to one's interactions with others and enemies.

topics.title: Four Therefores in Romans
topics.summary: Romans 12 has four 'therefore' statements that establish a chain of relationships, starting with the condemnation of the world, leading to justification, assurance, and finally, dedication.
key_points: Romans 3:20 is the 'therefore' of condemnation: the whole world is guilty before God.
Romans 5:1 is the 'therefore' of justification.
Romans 8:1 is the 'therefore' of assurance.
Romans 12:1 is the 'therefore' of dedication, serving as the basis for other relationships.

topics.title: Body as Living Sacrifice
topics.summary: Your body is a living sacrifice requiring two examples of living sacrifice: Isaac, who died in obedience, and Jesus Christ, who died in sacrifice.
key_points: Your body is a living sacrifice to give to God.
Isaac would have died in obedience to God, yielding to God’s will.
Jesus Christ actually died in sacrifice.

topics.title: Mind as Sacrifice
topics.summary: Your mind is a sacrifice to God because the Holy Spirit changes your mind by releasing internal power, allowing you to be a transformer rather than a conformer.
key_points: The world wants to change your mind with external pressure.
The Holy Spirit changes your mind by releasing power within.
If God controls your thinking, you are a transformer; if the world is in control, you are a conformer.
Meditating on God’s Word and memorization makes you more spiritual.

topics.title: Will as Sacrifice
topics.summary: Your will is a sacrifice to God, and yielding your will to God's power through disciplined prayer gives you willpower.
key_points: Your mind controls your body, and your will controls your mind.
Yielding your will to God allows His power to take over, giving you 'willpower'.
Surrender happens through disciplined prayer.
Pray about everything and yield the plans of the day to Him.

topics.title: Relationships with Believers
topics.summary: This section covers honest evaluation of spiritual gifts and ministries, faithful cooperation with others, and loving participation characterized by honest, humble love.
key_points: Each Christian must identify the spiritual gifts and ministry one is called to, being honest about self-evaluation.
Gifts are tools to build with, not toys to play with or weapons to fight with.
Work with others even if you don't like them or don't get along.
Love is the circulatory system of the spiritual body; it must be honest, not hypocritical, humble, and not proud.
Be joyful in hope, patient in affliction, and faithful in prayer, and share the burdens of others.
